node_phytochrome_pr_pfr.title: Phytochromes (phyA–phyE): Red (660 nm) vs. Far-Red (730 nm) Reversible Switch
node_phytochrome_pr_pfr.subtitle: Phytochromobilin C15=C16 Cis-to-Trans Photoisomerization, Nuclear Import & PIF Degradation

metrics.chromophore: Phytochromobilin (Linear tetrapyrrole covalently linked via a thioether bond to a conserved Cysteine in the GAF domain)
metrics.photoconversion: Pr (Inactive, λmax = 660 nm Red, C15-Z/cis) <-> Pfr (Biologically Active, λmax = 730 nm Far-Red, C15-E/trans)
metrics.types: Type I = phyA (Light-labile; mediates VLFR & Far-Red HIR) | Type II = phyB–phyE (Light-stable; phyB mediates Red/Far-Red LFR & Shade Avoidance)
metrics.downstream_targets: Active Pfr enters nucleus -> inhibits PIFs (bHLH repressors) AND inhibits COP1-SPA1 E3 ligase to stabilize HY5!

mechanism: Phytochromes are soluble homodimeric chromoproteins (~250 kDa) synthesized in the dark in their inactive **Red-absorbing $P_r$ state** ($\lambda_{\max} = 660\ \text{nm}$) in the cytosol.

1. **PHOTOISOMERIZATION**: Absorption of **Red light (660 nm)** causes the linear tetrapyrrole chromophore (**Phytochromobilin**) to isomerize from the *C15-Z (cis)* to the *C15-E (trans)* configuration at the C15=C16 double bond, converting the protein into the biologically active **Far-Red-absorbing $P_{fr}$ state** ($\lambda_{\max} = 730\ \text{nm}$). Absorption of **Far-Red light (730 nm)** (or slow thermal 'Dark Reversion') converts $P_{fr}$ back to inactive $P_r$.

2. **NUCLEAR TRANSLOCATION & DE-ETIOLATION**: Active **$P_{fr}$** exposes a nuclear localization signal (or binds FHY1/FHL for phyA) and translocates into the **Nucleus**, where it executes two master actions:
• Directly binds and triggers the phosphorylation and **26S proteasomal destruction of PIFs** (Phytochrome-Interacting Factors, which promote dark skotomorphogenesis/hypocotyl elongation).

• Disrupts the **COP1–SPA1 E3 Ubiquitin Ligase complex** (which in the dark degrades positive photomorphogenesis transcription factors like **HY5**), allowing **HY5** to accumulate and drive leaf greening, chloroplast development, and de-etiolation!
csir_high_yield: Guaranteed CSIR NET Part B & C Questions on Phytochrome Modes & Mutants:
• **Three Fluence Response Modes**:

1. **VLFR (Very Low Fluence Response)**: Mediated by **phyA** ($0.0001\text{ to }0.05\ \mu\text{mol m}^{-2}$); obeys the **Law of Reciprocity**, and **CANNOT be reversed by Far-Red light** (because even Far-Red light alone converts enough $P_r$ to the 0.02% $P_{fr}$ needed to trigger VLFR!).

2. **LFR (Low Fluence Response)**: Mediated primarily by **phyB** ($1\text{ to }1,000\ \mu\text{mol m}^{-2}$, e.g., lettuce seed germination); obeys Reciprocity, and is **100% Photoreversible by Red / Far-Red flashes** (**only the FINAL flash in a sequence of R–FR–R–FR determines the response!**).

3. **HIR (High Irradiance Response)**: Requires continuous, prolonged high-fluence exposure; **does NOT obey Reciprocity** and is **NOT photoreversible** (**phyA** mediates **Far-Red HIR** in de-etiolating seedlings; **phyB** mediates **Red HIR**).
• **phyA vs. phyB Mutant Hypocotyl Phenotypes (Classic CSIR Experimental Table!)**:

– ***phyA-* Null Mutant**: Shows an elongated (tall, etiolated) hypocotyl specifically under **Continuous Far-Red Light (FRc)**, but looks completely normal (short hypocotyl) under Continuous Red Light!

– ***phyB-* Null Mutant**: Shows an elongated (constitutive shade-avoidance) hypocotyl specifically under **Continuous Red Light (Rc)** or White Light, but looks normal under Continuous Far-Red Light!

– ***cop1-* or *det1-* Loss-of-Function Mutant**: Exhibits **constitutive photomorphogenesis in COMPLETE DARKNESS** (short hypocotyl, open cotyledons, and expression of light-regulated genes in the dark!).
pathology: Agricultural Shade Avoidance Syndrome (SAS): Under a dense crop canopy, upper leaves absorb Red light (660 nm) via chlorophyll while transmitting/reflecting Far-Red light (730 nm). The resulting **Low Red : Far-Red Ratio (Low R:FR)** shifts phyB into the inactive $P_r$ form, releasing **PIF4/PIF5/PIF7** to drive auxin synthesis (*TAA1/YUCCA*) and wasteful stem elongation at the expense of grain/tuber yield!
lab_workbench: Dual-Wavelength Difference Spectrophotometry ($\Delta(\Delta A) = \Delta A_{660} - \Delta A_{730}$): Measures photoreversible absorbance changes in etiolated oat coleoptile extracts after alternating actinic Red and Far-Red illumination (maximum photoequilibrium in pure Red light establishes $P_{fr} / P_{\text{total}} = \Phi \approx 0.85$ [85%], never 100%, due to overlapping absorption spectra!).

node_blue_light_receptors.subtitle: FAD/Pterin Photolyase Homologs (De-etiolation/Clock) vs. LOV-Domain Kinases (Phototropism/Chloroplast Movement)

metrics.blue_light_spectrum: 400–500 nm containing the signature 'Three-Finger' action spectrum peak (420, 450, 480 nm)
metrics.cryptochromes_cry1_2: Nuclear/Cytosolic proteins binding FAD + MTHF (Pterin); structurally homologous to DNA Photolyase but LACK DNA repair activity!
metrics.phototropins_phot1_2: Plasma-membrane Ser/Thr Kinases containing two N-terminal LOV domains (LOV1 & LOV2) binding FMN
metrics.zeitlupe_family: ZTL / FKF1 / LKP2 (Combine a LOV blue-light sensor with an F-box E3 ubiquitin ligase domain for circadian clock & flowering!)

mechanism: Plants perceive Blue and UV-A light ($320\text{–}500\ \text{nm}$) using three distinct photoreceptor classes:

1. **CRYPTOCHROMES (CRY1 & CRY2)**: Bind two chromophores: **FAD** (flavin adenine dinucleotide) and **MTHF** (pterin). Blue light induces FAD photoreduction and homodimerization, allowing CRY1/2 to bind **SPA1/COP1** in the nucleus—protecting **HY5** (to inhibit hypocotyl elongation and induce anthocyanin synthesis) and **CONSTANS (CO)** (to promote photoperiodic flowering) from degradation!

2. **PHOTOTROPINS (PHOT1 & PHOT2)**: Plasma-membrane-associated autophosphorylating **Serine/Threonine Kinases** containing two **LOV (Light-Oxygen-Voltage) domains**, each binding **FMN (Flavin Mononucleotide)**. Blue light induces a **covalent thiol-adduct bond** between a conserved Cysteine in the LOV2 domain and the C(4a) carbon of FMN, unfolding the $J\alpha$-helix to activate the C-terminal kinase domain! Mediates **Phototropism** (via asymmetric PIN3 auxin redistribution), **Stomatal Opening** (activating the PM $\text{H}^+$-ATPase via 14-3-3 binding), and **Chloroplast Movement**.

3. **UVR8 (UV-B Receptor, 280–315 nm)**: Uses intrinsic **Tryptophan** residues (Trp-285/Trp-233) as its chromophore without any prosthetic group! UV-B breaks salt bridges, monomerizing the UVR8 homodimer so it enters the nucleus and binds COP1 to activate HY5 and UV-protective flavonoid sunscreen synthesis.
csir_high_yield: Division of Labor Between PHOT1 and PHOT2 in Chloroplast Movement & Phototropism (Guaranteed CSIR NET Part C Question!):

• **Low-Fluence Blue Light**: Both **PHOT1 and PHOT2** mediate **Chloroplast Accumulation Response** (chloroplasts move to the flat periclinal walls parallel to the leaf surface to maximize light capture), and **PHOT1** mediates **low-light hypocotyl phototropism**.

• **High-Fluence Blue Light**: **PHOT2 ALONE** mediates the **Chloroplast Avoidance Response** (chloroplasts flee to the vertical anticlinal side walls via CHUP1 actin filaments to prevent photodamage!). Therefore, a ***phot2-* single mutant** shows normal accumulation in weak light, **but fails to show chloroplast avoidance in strong blue light** (and suffers severe photodamage)!

• **Blue-Light Stomatal Opening**: Driven by **Phototropins (PHOT1/PHOT2)** activating the guard cell plasma-membrane $\text{H}^+$-ATPase (**AHA1** phosphorylated + **14-3-3** bound) AND by guard-cell chloroplast **Zeaxanthin**.
pathology: Solar UV-B Crop Stress: Mutants lacking *UVR8* or chalcone synthase (*tt4*) cannot synthesize epidermal kaempferol/quercetin flavonoid sunscreens, suffering lethal cyclobutane pyrimidine dimer accumulation under natural sunlight.
lab_workbench: Optogenetics in Mammalian Neurobiology & Cell Biology: The **Arabidopsis PHOT1 LOV2-$J\alpha$ domain** and **CRY2–CIB1** blue-light dimerizers are the foundational molecular switches engineered into modern optogenetic tools to control protein localization and gene expression with laser beams in animal cells!

node_photoperiod_florigen_flc.title: Photoperiodism (External Coincidence Model), Florigen (FT) & Epigenetic Vernalization (FLC)
node_photoperiod_florigen_flc.subtitle: CONSTANS (CO) Stabilization by FKF1/CRY2/phyA, Phloem FT Transport & PRC2 H3K27me3 Cold Silencing

metrics.site_of_perception_vs_response: Photoperiod is perceived by mature LEAVES; floral transition occurs at the Shoot Apical Meristem (SAM)
metrics.external_coincidence_hub: CONSTANS (CO) mRNA peaks 12–16 hours after dawn; CO protein is stabilized ONLY if Light coincides with this peak!
metrics.mobile_florigen: FLOWERING LOCUS T (FT in Arabidopsis; Hd3a in Rice) — 20 kDa protein translated in leaf phloem companion cells, moves to SAM, binds FD + 14-3-3
metrics.vernalization_repressor: FLOWERING LOCUS C (FLC — MADS-box repressor of FT & SOC1); silenced by prolonged winter cold via VIN3 + PRC2 (H3K27me3)

mechanism: **THE EXTERNAL COINCIDENCE MODEL OF PHOTOPERIODISM (In Long-Day *Arabidopsis*)**:
1. The circadian clock drives transcription of **CONSTANS (*CO*) mRNA** so that it peaks strictly in the **late afternoon (12–16 hours after dawn)**.

2. **In Short Days (It is DARK at hour 12–16)**: In the dark, the nuclear **COP1–SPA1** E3 ligase rapidly ubiquitinates and destroys CO protein, while morning **phyB** also degrades CO $\rightarrow$ **No Flowering**.

3. **In Long Days (It is still LIGHT at hour 12–16)**: Late-afternoon Blue and Far-Red light activate **FKF1** (which degrades the *CO* transcriptional repressor **CDF1**), while **CRY2 and phyA** inhibit COP1 and stabilize **CO protein**! Accumulated CO activates transcription of **FLOWERING LOCUS T (*FT*)** in leaf phloem companion cells.

4. **FLORIGEN TRANSPORT TO THE SAM**: **FT protein** (not mRNA!) travels through the phloem sieve tubes to the Shoot Apical Meristem, where it forms the **Florigen Activation Complex (FT + 14-3-3 + bZIP transcription factor FD)** to activate floral meristem identity genes (**SOC1, APETALA1 [AP1], and LEAFY [LFY]**)!

**VERNALIZATION (Winter Cold Epigenetic Memory)**: Winter-annual *Arabidopsis* carries active **FRIGIDA (*FRI*)**, which drives high expression of the MADS-box floral repressor **FLOWERING LOCUS C (*FLC*)** (blocking *FT* and *SOC1*). Prolonged winter cold ($4^\circ\text{C}$ for 4–6 weeks) induces **COOLAIR/COLDAIR lncRNAs** and **VIN3**, which recruit **Polycomb Repressive Complex 2 (PRC2)** to deposit repressive **H3K27me3** across the *FLC* locus—mitotically silencing *FLC* throughout spring, until the mark is erased/reset during embryogenesis in the next generation!
csir_high_yield: High-Yield CSIR NET Questions on Night-Break Experiments & Short-Day vs. Long-Day Plants:

• **What do Plants Actually Measure—Day Length or NIGHT Length?** Classic **Hamner & Bonner Cocklebur (*Xanthium*) Experiments** proved that plants measure the duration of the **UNINTERRUPTED DARK PERIOD (Critical Night Length)**!
• **Night-Break Flash Rule (Red vs. Far-Red)**:

– Interrupting a long inductive night with a brief flash of **Red Light (660 nm)** **INHIBITS flowering in Short-Day Plants (SDP** like Rice, Soybean, *Xanthium*, *Pharbitis*) and **PROMOTES flowering in Long-Day Plants (LDP** like *Arabidopsis*, Wheat, Spinach, *Hyoscyamus*)!
– Immediately following the Red flash with a **Far-Red Flash (730 nm)** completely **REVERSES** the night-break effect—proving **Phytochrome** controls the night-break response!

• **Why does a Short-Day Plant like Rice (*Oryza sativa*) flower in Short Days when it uses the exact same *CO $\rightarrow$ FT* pathway?** In Rice, the *CO* homolog (**Hd1**) acts as a **bifunctional switch**: in **Short Days** (dark at peak), Hd1 **ACTIVATES** the *FT* homolog (**Hd3a**), whereas in **Long Days** (light at peak, interacting with $P_{fr}$), Hd1 converts into a **REPRESSOR** of *Hd3a*!
pathology: Crop Latitudinal Adaptation: Natural loss-of-function alleles in *Hd1*, *Ghd7*, or *PRR37* reduce photoperiod sensitivity in elite rice and wheat cultivars, allowing tropical short-day crops to flower and set grain during the long summer days of northern temperate latitudes.
lab_workbench: Chailakhyan's Inter-Species Grafting & *SUC2::FT-GFP* Phloem Mobility Assay: Grafting a single photo-induced leaf from a Short-Day Plant onto a Long-Day Plant kept in non-inductive short days induces the Long-Day Plant to flower—proving that the transmissible **Florigen (FT protein)** is universal across SDP and LDP species!

node_auxin_tir1_pin.title: Auxin (IAA): Polar Chemiosmotic Transport (PIN/AUX1), SCF-TIR1 Degron & Acid Growth
node_auxin_tir1_pin.subtitle: Tryptophan-to-IAA (TAA1/YUCCA), Polar Basal PIN Efflux, Aux/IAA Ubiquitination & PM H+-ATPase Loosening

metrics.biosynthesis_main: Tryptophan-Dependent IPyA Pathway: Trp -> Indole-3-Pyruvate (via TAA1 aminotransferase) -> IAA (via YUCCA flavin monooxygenase)
metrics.polar_transport_carriers: Influx: Passive IAAH (apoplast pH 5.5) + Active AUX1/LAX (2 H+/IAA- symporter) | Efflux: Basal PIN1–7 (driven by ΔΨ inside-negative!) + ABCB
metrics.nuclear_receptor: SCF^(TIR1/AFB) E3 Ubiquitin Ligase (Auxin acts as 'molecular glue' between TIR1 F-box and Domain II of Aux/IAA repressors)
metrics.acid_growth_wall: TMK1 / SAUR19 inhibit PP2C.D phosphatase -> Activates AHA PM H+-ATPase -> Apoplast pH drops to 4.5 -> Activates Expansins!

mechanism: **1. THE CHEMIOSMOTIC POLAR AUXIN TRANSPORT MODEL (Goldsmith / Rubery & Sheldrake)**:

• In the acidic **Cell Wall / Apoplast (pH ~5.0–5.5)**, ~15–25% of Indole-3-Acetic Acid ($\text{p}K_a = 4.75$) is protonated neutral **IAAH** (which diffuses passively across the lipid bilayer) while ~75–85% is anionic **$\text{IAA}^-$** (actively imported via the **AUX1/LAX $2\text{H}^+/\text{IAA}^-$ symporter**).

• Once inside the neutral **Cytosol (pH ~7.2)**, >99% of IAA dissociates into membrane-impermeable anionic **$\text{IAA}^-$** (**Anion Trap!**). Therefore, $\text{IAA}^-$ can **ONLY exit the cell where PIN efflux carriers are localized**! Because **PIN1** is localized specifically to the **basal (lower) plasma membrane** of shoot vascular parenchyma cells (trafficked dynamically via **GNOM ARF-GEF** endosomal recycling), auxin flows strictly unidirectionally from shoot apex to root (**Basipetal** in shoot; **Acropetal** into the root tip via PIN1, then **Basipetal/Shootward** in the outer root epidermis via PIN2!).
**2. NUCLEAR $\text{SCF}^{\text{TIR1/AFB}}$ DE-REPRESSION SIGNALING**:

• **Low Auxin**: **Aux/IAA** repressor proteins dimerize (via PB1 domains) with DNA-bound **ARF** (Auxin Response Factor) transcription factors and recruit the corepressor **TOPLESS (TPL)** + HDACs to silence auxin genes.

• **High Auxin**: IAA binds inside the bottom of the leucine-rich-repeat pocket of the F-box protein **TIR1 / AFB**, acting as **'molecular glue'** that creates a high-affinity binding surface for the conserved **GWPPV 'degron' motif (Domain II)** of **Aux/IAA**! $\text{SCF}^{\text{TIR1}}$ polyubiquitinates Aux/IAA for **26S proteasomal destruction**, liberating **ARF** to transcribe early auxin genes (*Aux/IAA, GH3, SAUR*)!

**3. THE ACID-GROWTH HYPOTHESIS (Rapid Cell Elongation)**: Auxin-induced **SAUR** proteins bind and **inhibit PP2C.D phosphatases**, keeping the plasma-membrane **$\text{H}^+$-ATPase (AHA1/2)** phosphorylated and active. Extruded $\text{H}^+$ acidifies the cell wall to **pH 4.5**, activating **Expansins** (which disrupt non-covalent hydrogen bonds between cellulose microfibrils and xyloglucan hemicelluloses without hydrolyzing them!), allowing turgor pressure to stretch the cell wall!
csir_high_yield: High-Yield CSIR NET Experimental Scenarios on Auxin Mutants & Inhibitors:

• **Gain-of-Function Dominant Mutation in Aux/IAA Domain II (e.g., *axr2-1* / *shy2* / *bdl* — GWPPVDegron Mutation)**: What happens if a point mutation alters the **GWPPV degron sequence in Domain II of an Aux/IAA repressor**? TIR1 can **NO LONGER bind or ubiquitinate** the mutant Aux/IAA protein even when Auxin is high! The mutant Aux/IAA protein becomes indestructible and permanently represses ARFs, causing a **Dominant Auxin-Insensitive phenotype**! (Conversely, deleting the F-box of TIR1 is a *recessive* loss-of-function).

• **Polar Auxin Transport Inhibitors (NPA & TIBA)**: **NPA** (1-N-naphthylphthalamic acid) and **TIBA** (2,3,5-triiodobenzoic acid) block **PIN/ABCB auxin efflux** without blocking influx—abolishing phototropism, gravitropism, and lateral root formation!

• **Fusicoccin (Fungal Toxin from *Fusicoccum amygdali*)**: Irreversibly locks the **14-3-3 protein** onto the C-terminus of the plasma-membrane **$\text{H}^+$-ATPase**, causing massive, auxin-independent cell wall acidification, super-elongation, and irreversible stomatal opening!
pathology: Synthetic Auxin Herbicides (**2,4-D** [2,4-Dichlorophenoxyacetic acid] and **Dicamba**): Selectively kill **broadleaf Dicot weeds** while sparing **Monocot cereal crops** (wheat, maize, rice) because monocots rapidly inactivate 2,4-D via ring-hydroxylation/conjugation and have different vascular/auxin-receptor sensitivities.
lab_workbench: *DR5::GUS* / *DR5::GFP* Synthetic Auxin-Response Reporter & *DII-VENUS* Degron Sensor: **DR5** (tandem repeats of the `5'-TGTCTC-3'` ARF-binding AuxRE element) glows bright green where auxin transcriptional output is high (e.g., quiescent center & lower side of gravistimulated roots), while **DII-VENUS** (Domain II of Aux/IAA fused to yellow fluorescent protein) is **rapidly degraded within minutes** wherever auxin enters!

node_gibberellin_gid1_della.title: Gibberellins (GA1/GA3/GA4): GID1–SCF^(SLY1)–DELLA Signaling, Green Revolution & Seed Aleurone
node_gibberellin_gid1_della.subtitle: Terpenoid Diterpene Biosynthesis, Allosteric GID1 Lid Closing & Cereal α-Amylase GAMYB Activation

metrics.biosynthetic_pathway: Diterpenoid (C20/C19) via Plastid MEP Pathway: GGDP -> ent-Kaurene (Plastid) -> GA12 (ER P450s) -> Active GA1/GA4 (Cytosol GA20ox & GA3ox)
metrics.active_vs_inactive_ga: Bioactive GAs require 3β-hydroxylation (catalyzed by GA 3-oxidase / *Le* gene in Mendel's tall/dwarf peas!); GA 2-oxidase INACTIVATES GA!
metrics.receptor_repressor_complex: Soluble Receptor GID1 + Bioactive GA -> Closes N-terminal lid to bind DELLA repressor (GAI, RGA, Rht, SLR1) -> Ubiquitinated by SCF^(SLY1/GID2)
metrics.seed_germination_axis: Embryo secretes GA -> Scutellum -> Aleurone Layer -> Destroys SLN1/DELLA -> Induces GAMYB -> Secretes α-Amylase into starchy endosperm!

mechanism: **BIOSYNTHESIS ACROSS THREE COMPARTMENTS**: Synthesized from **Geranylgeranyl Diphosphate (GGDP, 20C)** in **Plastids** ($\rightarrow$ *ent*-Kaurene; inhibited by **AMO-1618** and **CCC/Chlormequat**), oxidized on the **ER membrane** by cytochrome P450 monooxygenases ($\rightarrow \text{GA}_{12}$; inhibited by **Paclobutrazol** and **Ancymidol**), and converted into bioactive $\text{GA}_1$ and $\text{GA}_4$ in the **Cytosol** by 2-oxoglutarate-dependent dioxygenases (**GA20ox** and **GA3ox**).
**NUCLEAR GID1–DELLA DE-REPRESSION MECHANISM**:

• Unlike Auxin (where IAA glues the repressor directly to the F-box protein), **Gibberellin binds deep inside the pocket of a separate soluble nuclear receptor called GID1** (a hormone-sensitive lipase homolog).

• GA binding causes an N-terminal alpha-helical **'Lid' on GID1 to snap shut** over the GA pocket. The closed outer surface of this GID1 lid specifically recognizes the conserved N-terminal **DELLA/TVHYNP domain** of nuclear **DELLA growth-repressor proteins** (**GAI, RGA** in *Arabidopsis*; **Rht-1** in Wheat; **SLR1** in Rice).

• Once locked onto GID1-GA, the DELLA protein's C-terminal GRAS domain is recognized by the **$\text{SCF}^{\text{SLY1/GID2}}$ E3 Ubiquitin Ligase**, polyubiquitinated, and destroyed by the 26S proteasome—releasing PIFs and GAMYB to drive stem internode elongation and seed germination!
csir_high_yield: Norman Borlaug's 'Green Revolution' Semi-Dwarf Wheat vs. Rice Genes (Top CSIR NET Unit 6 & Unit 8 Integration!):

• **Green Revolution Wheat (*Rht-B1b / Rht-D1b*) & Maize (*Dwarf8*)**: Carry a **DOMINANT Gain-of-Function deletion in the N-terminal DELLA domain** of the DELLA repressor! Because the DELLA domain is mutated, GID1-GA **cannot bind or degrade** the Rht repressor. Therefore, *Rht* wheat is **GA-INSENSITIVE** (spraying exogenous $\text{GA}_3$ CANNOT rescue its height!).

• **Green Revolution Rice (*sd1 — Semi-Dwarf 1*) & Gregor Mendel's Dwarf Pea (*le*)**: Carry a **RECESSIVE Loss-of-Function mutation in a GA Biosynthetic Enzyme** (**GA 20-oxidase [*sd1*]** in Rice; **GA 3-oxidase [*le*]** in Mendel's Pea)! Because their GID1 receptor and DELLA signaling machinery are 100% intact, **spraying exogenous $\text{GA}_3$ completely RESCUES *sd1* rice and Mendel's *le/le* dwarf pea back to full wild-type tall height!**

• **Cereal Aleurone Layer $\alpha$-Amylase Assay**: De-embryonated barley half-seeds lack the embryo (the natural source of GA); adding nanomolar exogenous $\text{GA}_3$ triggers **SLN1 (DELLA) degradation** within 10 minutes $\rightarrow$ early transcription of the primary response gene **GAMYB** (insensitive to cycloheximide, though GAMYB protein translation requires ribosomes) $\rightarrow$ GAMYB binds the `5'-TAACAAA-3'` gibberellin-response element on the **$\alpha$-Amylase** promoter (antagonized by **ABA**, which induces PKABA1 kinase to block GAMYB!).
pathology: *Gibberella fujikuroi* (*Fusarium*) 'Bakanae' (Foolish Seedling) Disease of Rice: The pathogenic fungus secretes massive quantities of **Gibberellic Acid ($\text{GA}_3$)** into infected rice seedlings, causing hyper-elongated, pale, lodge-prone stems that collapse before setting grain.

metrics.ja_biosynthesis: Octadecanoid Pathway from α-Linolenic Acid (18:3): Chloroplast (LOX, AOS, AOC -> OPDA) -> Peroxisome (OPDA Reductase OPR3 + 3 β-Oxidations -> JA) -> Cytosol (JAR1 conjugates Isoleucine -> Active (+)-7-iso-JA-Ile!)
metrics.ja_receptor_complex: SCF^(COI1) F-box + JAZ Repressor + Inositol Pentakisphosphate (InsP5 cofactor) -> Destroys JAZ -> Releases MYC2!
metrics.strigolactone_axis: Carotenoid-derived hormone (CCD7/CCD8) -> D14 receptor (α/β-hydrolase that hydrolyzes SL!) + SCF^(MAX2/D3) -> Destroys SMXL6/7/8 / D53 to INHIBIT axillary bud outgrowth!

mechanism: **JASMONATE (JA-Ile) BIOSYNTHESIS & $\text{SCF}^{\text{COI1}}$ SIGNALING (Herbivore & Necrotroph Defense)**:

1. Chewing insects or mechanical wounding release **$\alpha$-Linolenic Acid (18:3)** from chloroplast membranes. Lipoxygenase (LOX), Allene Oxide Synthase (AOS), and Allene Oxide Cyclase (AOC) convert it into **12-oxo-phytodienoic acid (OPDA)** inside the **Chloroplast**. OPDA moves to the **Peroxisome**, where **OPR3** and three rounds of $\beta$-oxidation yield Jasmonic Acid (JA). Finally, in the **Cytosol**, **JAR1** conjugates JA to the amino acid **Isoleucine** to create the sole bioactive ligand: **(+)-7-*iso*-Jasmonoyl-L-Isoleucine (JA-Ile)**!

2. In uninjured cells, **JAZ (Jasmonate ZIM-Domain)** repressors bind and inhibit the master transcription factor **MYC2** (recruiting NINJA + TOPLESS). Upon wounding, **JA-Ile** acts as molecular glue between the F-box protein **COI1 (Coronatine Insensitive 1)** and the **Jas domain of JAZ**, triggering JAZ proteasomal degradation and unleashing **MYC2** to transcribe **Proteinase Inhibitors (Pin1/Pin2)**, glucosinolates, and alkaloids that poison insect midguts!
**STRIGOLACTONE SIGNALING (Shoot Branching Inhibition & Mycorrhizal Attraction)**:

Synthesized in roots from $\beta$-carotene (**carlactone** pathway via **CCD7 [*MAX3*], CCD8 [*MAX4*], and MAX1**). Perceived by **D14** (an $\alpha/\beta$-hydrolase receptor that **enzymatically cleaves Strigolactone** and traps the D-ring covalently!) + **$\text{SCF}^{\text{MAX2/D3}}$**, which degrades **D53 / SMXL6,7,8** repressors to upregulate *BRC1* and **inhibit axillary shoot branching**!
csir_high_yield: High-Yield CSIR NET Questions on Bacterial Coronatine Mimicry & SA–JA Antagonism:

• **How does the hemibiotrophic bacterial pathogen *Pseudomonas syringae* trick the plant into opening closed stomata and suppressing Salicylic Acid immunity?** *P. syringae* secretes the phytotoxin **Coronatine (COR)**—a dead-ringer structural mimic of **JA-Ile** that binds **COI1–JAZ** with 100x higher affinity than endogenous JA-Ile! By hyperactivating the **JA / MYC2 pathway**, Coronatine **antagonizes and shuts down the Salicylic Acid (SA) pathway** (which the plant needs to fight biotrophic *P. syringae*) AND forces guard cells to reopen stomata so bacteria can invade the leaf!

• **Therefore, what is the phenotype of an *Arabidopsis coi1-* loss-of-function mutant when infected with *Pseudomonas syringae*?** Paradoxically, ***coi1-* mutants are HYPER-RESISTANT to *Pseudomonas syringae*** (because Coronatine has no receptor to bind, leaving Salicylic Acid immunity at 100%!), while being hyper-susceptible to chewing caterpillars and necrotrophic fungi (*Botrytis*) and **male-sterile** (defective anther filament elongation and pollen dehiscence)!

• **Why do roots exude Strigolactones into the soil under Phosphate starvation?** To attract beneficial **Arbuscular Mycorrhizal (AM) Fungi** (stimulating hyphal branching)—a signal hijacked over evolution by parasitic weeds ***Striga* (Witchweed)** and ***Orobanche* (Broomrape)** to trigger seed germination only when a host root is millimeters away!
pathology: *Striga hermonthica* Parasitic Weed Infestation: Devastates cereal crops (*Sorghum, Zea mays*, Millet) across Africa and Asia; low-strigolactone-exuding sorghum alleles (*lgs1*) confer field resistance to *Striga*.

metrics.biosynthesis_oxidation: Synthesized by IPT (Isopentenyl Transferase: DMAPP + AMP/ADP/ATP -> iPMP -> trans-Zeatin via CYP735A); degraded irreversibly by Cytokinin Oxidase (CKX)

mechanism: **MULTI-STEP TWO-COMPONENT PHOSPHORELAY (Bacterial Homology)**:

1. **Receptor Activation**: Bioactive cytokinins (*trans*-Zeatin, Isopentenyladenine) bind the CHASE domain of transmembrane hybrid **Histidine Kinase Receptors (CRE1/AHK4, AHK2, AHK3)** localized on the **ER and Plasma Membrane**. Cytokinin binding stimulates autophosphorylation of a conserved **Histidine (His)** residue, followed by intramolecular transfer of the phosphate to a receiver **Aspartate (Asp)** on the same receptor.

2. **AHP Nuclear Shuttle**: The phosphate is transferred to a conserved **Histidine** on a small cytosolic shuttle protein called **AHP (Arabidopsis Histidine Phosphotransfer protein, AHP1–5)**, which translocates through the nuclear pore into the nucleus. *(Note: **AHP6** lacks the conserved Histidine and acts as a dominant-negative inhibitor of cytokinin signaling in protoxylem differentiation!).*
3. **Nuclear ARR Switch (Type-B vs. Type-A)**:

• **Type-B ARRs (ARR1, ARR10, ARR12)**: Contain both an Asp receiver domain AND a **GARP/MYB DNA-binding transactivation domain**. Phosphorylation by AHP relieves autoinhibition, allowing Type-B ARRs to activate cytokinin target genes (including *WUSCHEL* in the shoot meristem, *CYCD3* for cell division, and *Type-A ARRs*!).

• **Type-A ARRs (ARR4, ARR5, ARR6, ARR7, ARR15)**: Contain an Asp receiver domain but **LACK a DNA-binding domain**! Rapidly transcribed by Type-B ARRs, Type-A ARRs compete for phosphoryl groups from AHPs to provide **negative feedback** (and *ARR7/ARR15* are repressed by Auxin/MP in the SAM!).
csir_high_yield: High-Yield CSIR NET Rules on Skoog & Miller Callus Organogenesis & Agrobacterium Crown Gall:
• **Skoog & Miller Auxin : Cytokinin Ratio Rule in Tissue Culture**:
– **High Auxin : Low Cytokinin Ratio** $\rightarrow$ Induces **ROOT** differentiation (Rhizogenesis).
– **Low Auxin : High Cytokinin Ratio** $\rightarrow$ Induces **SHOOT** differentiation (Caulogenesis).
– **Intermediate / Balanced Auxin : Cytokinin** $\rightarrow$ Proliferates as undifferentiated **Callus**.

• **Agrobacterium tumefaciens Ti-Plasmid T-DNA Oncogenes (Unit 6 + Unit 12 Integration!)**: Wild-type T-DNA integrates three hormone biosynthetic genes into the plant genome: ***iaaM* (tms1, Tryptophan monooxygenase) + *iaaH* (tms2, Indoleacetamide hydrolase)** [synthesize **Auxin**], and ***ipt* (tmr, Isopentenyl transferase)** [synthesizes **Cytokinin**].
– **Wild-Type Ti Plasmid** $\rightarrow$ Unorganized **Crown Gall Tumor** (grows on hormone-free medium!).
– **Mutant in *iaaM/iaaH* ('Shooter' Mutant — High Cytokinin : Low Auxin)** $\rightarrow$ Produces a teratoma tumor sprouting lush green **SHOOTS**!
– **Mutant in *ipt* ('Rooter' Mutant — High Auxin : Low Cytokinin)** $\rightarrow$ Produces a tumor covered in prolific **ROOTS**!

node_ethylene_etr1_ein2.subtitle: Cu+-Dependent Receptor Inactivation by Ethylene, EIN2 C-END Cleavage & The Seedling 'Triple Response'

metrics.yang_cycle_biosynthesis: Methionine -> SAM (via SAM Synthetase) -> ACC [1-Aminocyclopropane-1-Carboxylic Acid] (via ACS — Rate-Limiting!) -> Ethylene (via ACO + O2)
metrics.er_receptors_negative: ETR1, ETR2, ERS1, ERS2, EIN4 (ER-membrane homodimers requiring a Cu+ cofactor delivered by RAN1 P-type ATPase!)
metrics.signaling_topology: NEGATIVE REGULATORS: ETR1 & CTR1 (Raf-like kinase) and EBF1/2 (F-box) | POSITIVE REGULATORS: EIN2, EIN3/EIL1, ERF1
metrics.triple_response_dark: 1. Short/Stunted & Thickened (Radial Swelling) Hypocotyl + 2. Short Root + 3. Exaggerated Apical Hook!

mechanism: **BIOSYNTHESIS (THE YANG CYCLE)**: S-Adenosylmethionine (**SAM**) is converted into **ACC (1-aminocyclopropane-1-carboxylic acid)** by **ACC Synthase (ACS)** (a **PLP [Vitamin B6]-dependent** enzyme that is the **rate-limiting step**, stabilized via phosphorylation by MPK6 or cytokinin/auxin!). **ACC Oxidase (ACO)** then oxidizes ACC (requiring **$\text{O}_2$ and $\text{Fe}^{2+}$/Ascorbate**) into gaseous **Ethylene ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$)** + HCN + $\text{CO}_2$.
**INVERSE-AGONIST SIGNALING ON THE ER MEMBRANE (Why ETR1 is Active in the ABSENCE of Ethylene!)**:

• **IN AIR (NO ETHYLENE)**: The ER-membrane receptor **ETR1** is **ACTIVE** and activates the physically associated Raf-like Ser/Thr kinase **CTR1 (Constitutive Triple Response 1)**. Active **CTR1 phosphorylates the C-terminus of EIN2**, keeping EIN2 inactive on the ER membrane. Meanwhile in the nucleus, F-box proteins **EBF1/EBF2** constitutively ubiquitinate and destroy the transcription factor **EIN3** $\rightarrow$ **Ethylene genes OFF**!

• **WITH ETHYLENE GAS PRESENT**: Ethylene binds to the **$\text{Cu}^+$ cofactor** inside the transmembrane pocket of **ETR1**, which **TURNS OFF (INACTIVATES) ETR1 and CTR1**! Once CTR1 stops phosphorylating EIN2, the C-terminal domain of EIN2 (**EIN2-CEND**) is proteolytically cleaved off, inhibits *EBF1/2* mRNA translation in the cytosol, and translocates into the **Nucleus** to stabilize **EIN3 / EIL1**, which transcribe **ERF1** and ethylene response genes!
csir_high_yield: Genetic Epistasis & Mutant Phenotypes of the Ethylene Pathway (Arguably the #1 Most-Tested Signaling Question in CSIR NET Unit 6!):
• **Wait—why are *etr1-1* and *ein4-1* Ethylene-Insensitive mutants DOMINANT, whereas *ctr1-* is RECESSIVE?**

– Because the five ethylene receptors (ETR1, ETR2, ERS1, ERS2, EIN4) are redundant **negative regulators**! A single *recessive loss-of-function* knockout in *etr1* has no phenotype (the other 4 receptors still activate CTR1), whereas a **quadruple/quintuple loss-of-function knockout of all receptors shows a CONSTITUTIVE TRIPLE RESPONSE even in air**! Conversely, the classic ***etr1-1* point mutation (Cys65Tyr)** abolishes $\text{Cu}^+$ and ethylene binding so that **mutant ETR1-1 stays permanently ON (continuously activating CTR1) even when flooded with ethylene** $\rightarrow$ **Dominant Ethylene-Insensitive (Tall, no hook in ethylene)**!

– ***ctr1-* Loss-of-Function Mutant**: Recessive mutation that loses the CTR1 kinase brake $\rightarrow$ shows a **Constitutive Triple Response (short, fat hypocotyl with exaggerated hook) even in the complete absence of ethylene (and cannot be rescued by $\text{Ag}^+$ or 1-MCP!)**.
– ***ein2-* or *ein3-* Loss-of-Function Mutant**: Recessive **Ethylene-Insensitive** (Tall, thin hypocotyl even in high ethylene).

– ***eto1-* (Ethylene Overproducer 1) Mutant**: Overproduces ethylene gas (via stabilizing ACS5) $\rightarrow$ shows a Triple Response in air, **WHICH CAN BE RESCUED back to normal tall growth by adding $\text{Ag}^+$ (Silver thiosulfate) or AVG/AOA** (unlike *ctr1-*!).
• **Epistasis Rule**: What is the phenotype of a ***ctr1- ein2-* double mutant**? Because **EIN2 acts DOWNSTREAM of CTR1**, the double mutant is **Ethylene-Insensitive (Tall, looks like *ein2-*)**!
pathology: Post-Harvest Climacteric Fruit Ripening (Tomato, Banana, Apple, Mango, Avocado): Autocatalytic System-2 ethylene burst induces cell-wall-softening **Polygalacturonase** and **Pectin Methylesterase**. Tomato ***Never-ripe (Nr)*** carries a dominant ethylene-receptor mutation homologous to *etr1-1*, while antisense suppression of ACS/ACO creates non-softening slow-ripening tomatoes.
lab_workbench: Dark-Grown *Arabidopsis* Seedling Triple-Response Genetic Screen (Guzmán & Ecker) & Chemical Blockers:
• **Biosynthesis Inhibitors (Block ACS)**: **AVG (Aminoethoxyvinylglycine)** and **AOA (Aminooxyacetic acid)** inhibit PLP-dependent **ACC Synthase** (can be bypassed by adding exogenous **ACC**!).
• **Biosynthesis Inhibitor (Blocks ACO)**: **$\text{Co}^{2+}$ (Cobalt ions)** or anaerobiosis ($\text{N}_2$ atmosphere) blocks **ACC Oxidase**.

• **Receptor Action Antagonists (Block ETR1 $\text{Cu}^+$ site)**: **Silver ions ($\text{Ag}^+$ / Silver Thiosulfate, used by florists to stop carnation senescence!)**, **1-MCP (1-Methylcyclopropene)**, and *trans*-cyclooctene.

node_brassinosteroid_bri1.subtitle: Campesterol Steroid Hormone Perceived at the Plasma Membrane (Not Nucleus!) -> BZR1/BES1 Dephosphorylation

metrics.steroid_precursor: Campesterol (Plant sterol) -> Brassinolide (via DET2 5α-reductase [homolog of mammalian steroid 5α-reductase!] & CPD/DWF4 P450s)
metrics.surface_receptor: BRI1 (Brassinosteroid Insensitive 1 — LRR Receptor Ser/Thr Kinase) + Co-receptor BAK1 (SERK3)
metrics.negative_kinase: BIN2 (Brassinosteroid Insensitive 2 — a GSK3-like kinase that phosphorylates and INACTIVATES BZR1/BES1 in the absence of BR!)
metrics.positive_phosphatase_tf: BSU1 Phosphatase (Inactivates BIN2) + PP2A (Dephosphorylates BZR1 & BES1 so they activate BR target genes!)

mechanism: Unlike animal steroid hormones (estrogen, testosterone, cortisol), which diffuse through the plasma membrane to bind intracellular nuclear receptors, plant steroid hormones (**Brassinosteroids / Brassinolide**) are perceived **AT THE PLASMA MEMBRANE** by a transmembrane Leucine-Rich Repeat Receptor Kinase (**BRI1**)!
**STEP-BY-STEP SIGNALING CASCADE**:

1. **No Brassinosteroid (Basal State)**: BRI1 is held inactive by its C-terminal tail and the inhibitory protein **BKI1**. Meanwhile in the cytosol/nucleus, the constitutively active GSK3-like kinase **BIN2** phosphorylates the transcription factors **BZR1 and BES1**, causing them to be exported/sequestered in the cytosol by **14-3-3 proteins** and degraded by the proteasome.

2. **With Brassinolide Bound**: Brassinolide binds the extracellular island domain of **BRI1**, triggering phosphorylation and dissociation of **BKI1** and hetero-oligomerization/trans-phosphorylation with the co-receptor kinase **BAK1**. Activated BRI1 phosphorylates BSKs, which activate the phosphatase **BSU1**.

3. **Inactivation of BIN2 & Nuclear Activation**: **BSU1 dephosphorylates a conserved Tyrosine residue on BIN2, INACTIVATING BIN2**! Subsequently, **PP2A phosphatase** strips phosphates off **BZR1 and BES1**, allowing unphosphorylated BZR1/BES1 to accumulate in the nucleus and drive cell elongation, vascular xylem differentiation, and pollen tube growth!
csir_high_yield: High-Yield CSIR NET Traps on Brassinosteroid Mutants (*bri1*, *det2*, *bin2*):

• **Phenotype of Brassinosteroid Deficiency or Insensitivity**: Extreme **dwarfism ('cabbage-like' dark-green curled leaves)**, reduced apical dominance, delayed senescence, male sterility, and **de-etiolation in the dark** (short hypocotyl and open cotyledons in darkness, e.g., ***det2-***!).

• **Rescue Test (*det2-* vs. *bri1-*)**: Both *det2-* (lacks steroid $5\alpha$-reductase) and *bri1-* (lacks BRI1 receptor) are severe dark-green dwarfs; spraying exogenous **24-Epibrassinolide** completely rescues ***det2-*** to wild-type height, but has zero effect on ***bri1-***!

• **Why is the classic *bin2-1* mutant a DOMINANT dwarf that mimics *bri1-*?** Because **BIN2 is a negative regulator** (phosphorylates and inhibits BZR1/BES1); the *bin2-1* gain-of-function mutation prevents BSU1 from inactivating BIN2, permanently locking BZR1/BES1 in the inactive phosphorylated state! (Can be chemically bypassed in the lab by adding **Bikinin**, a direct small-molecule inhibitor of BIN2 kinase!).
pathology: Crop Lodging Resistance in Barley (*uzu* Semi-Dwarf Barley): A natural missense mutation in the barley *BRI1* homolog (*HvBRI1*) produces sturdy, erect-leaved semi-dwarf barley cultivars that capture light efficiently at high planting densities without lodging in heavy wind/rain.
lab_workbench: Rice Lamina Inclination Bioassay & BZR1-CFP Western Blot Mobility Shift: Applying nanogram quantities of Brassinolide to the junction between the rice leaf blade and leaf sheath causes dramatic adaxial cell expansion and **bending of the leaf lamina** away from the vertical axis (proporational to BR concentration); on SDS-PAGE, Brassinolide treatment shifts the upper phosphorylated BZR1 band down to the fast-migrating **dephosphorylated active BZR1** band!

node_aba_stomatal_guard_cell.title: Abscisic Acid (ABA): PYR/PYL–PP2C–SnRK2 Core Module & Guard Cell Stomatal Closure
node_aba_stomatal_guard_cell.subtitle: Carotenoid NCED Cleavage, PP2C (ABI1/2) Inhibition & SLAC1 Anion / K+ Efflux Turgor Collapse

metrics.biosynthesis_rate_limiting: C40 Carotenoid (Violaxanthin/Neoxanthin in Plastid) -> Cleaved by NCED (9-cis-Epoxycarotenoid Dioxygenase — Rate-Limiting!) -> Xanthoxin (C15) -> Cytosolic ABA
metrics.core_signaling_triad: 1. PYR/PYL/RCAR (Soluble Receptor) + ABA -> 2. Binds & INHIBITS PP2C Phosphatases (ABI1, ABI2, HAB1) -> 3. Releases SnRK2 Kinases (OST1 / SnRK2.6)!
metrics.guard_cell_channels: OST1 phosphorylates SLAC1 (S-type Anion Channel: Cl- & Malate2- efflux -> Depolarization!) + Inhibits KAT1 (K+in) + Activates GORK (K+out) -> Water exits via Aquaporins!
metrics.seed_dormancy_tf: SnRK2 phosphorylates bZIP transcription factors ABI5 / ABFs (bind ABRE elements) + ABI3 (VP1 in maize) to enforce seed dormancy & prevent Vivipary!

mechanism: **1. THE CORE ABA SIGNALING TRIAD (PYR/PYL – PP2C – SnRK2 Double-Negative Switch)**:

• **No ABA (Well-Watered)**: Group A **PP2C Protein Phosphatases (ABI1, ABI2, HAB1)** physically bind and dephosphorylate the activation loop of **SnRK2 Kinases (OST1 / SnRK2.2/2.3/2.6)**, keeping SnRK2 **OFF**.

• **With ABA (Drought / Osmotic Stress)**: ABA binds inside the START-domain pocket of soluble **PYR/PYL/RCAR** receptors, snapping a 'gate-and-latch' loop closed. The closed **PYR/PYL–ABA complex docks directly into the catalytic active site of PP2C (ABI1/ABI2), INHIBITING the phosphatase**! Released from PP2C inhibition, **SnRK2 (OST1)** autophosphorylates and switches **ON**!
**2. GUARD CELL STOMATAL CLOSURE MECHANICS (Step-by-Step Ion & Water Flux)**:

• Active **OST1 (SnRK2.6)** phosphorylates and activates NADPH oxidase (**RBOHD/F** $\rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ + $\text{NO}$ $\rightarrow$ triggers **$\text{Ca}^{2+}$ influx and tonoplast $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ release** via $\text{IP}_3/\text{cADPR}$) AND directly phosphorylates the plasma-membrane **Slow Anion Channel SLAC1** (and QUAC1).

• Massive **efflux of $\text{Cl}^-$ and $\text{Malate}^{2-}$** out of the guard cell (combined with ABA inhibition of the PM $\text{H}^+$-ATPase) causes rapid **Membrane Depolarization** (from $-120\ \text{mV}$ to $-30\ \text{mV}$).

• Membrane depolarization **closes inward-rectifying $\text{K}^+_{\text{in}}$ channels (KAT1)** and **opens outward-rectifying $\text{K}^+_{\text{out}}$ channels (GORK)**! Massive efflux of $\text{K}^+$ and $\text{Cl}^-$ raises guard cell $\Psi_s$ (less negative), causing water to rush out via PIP2;1 **Aquaporins**, collapsing guard cell turgor pressure ($\Psi_p$) and **closing the stomatal pore**!
csir_high_yield: High-Yield CSIR NET Questions on Root-to-Shoot pH Redistribution & *abi1-1* Dominance:

• **Why are the classic *abi1-1* and *abi2-1* (Gly180Asp) mutants DOMINANT ABA-insensitive 'wilty' mutants, whereas *abi1* null knockouts are hypersensitive to ABA?** Because **ABI1 and ABI2 are PP2C negative regulators**! The classic *abi1-1* (G180D) missense mutation prevents **PYR/PYL–ABA** from binding and inhibiting the ABI1 phosphatase, yet leaves ABI1's catalytic ability to dephosphorylate and shut off **SnRK2 (OST1)** completely intact—so mutant ABI1-1 dominantly keeps SnRK2 OFF even in high ABA!

• **Apoplastic pH Redistribution of ABA During Early Drought (Before De Novo Leaf Synthesis)**: In well-watered plants, xylem sap is slightly acidic (**pH ~6.0**); neutral protonated **ABAH** ($\text{p}K_a = 4.7$) is taken up and trapped inside alkaline mesophyll cells (cytosol pH 7.2) before reaching guard cells. At the very first sign of soil drying, xylem sap **alkalinizes to pH ~7.2**! At pH 7.2, ABA dissociates into membrane-impermeable anionic **$\text{ABA}^-$**, which cannot be absorbed by mesophyll cells along the way and travels straight through the apoplast to flood the **Guard Cells**!

• **Vivipary (Precocious Germination on the Mother Cob)**: Maize ***vp1* (viviparous-1, homolog of *Arabidopsis ABI3*)** or carotenoid-deficient ***vp5/vp14* (NCED)** mutants fail to synthesize or respond to ABA during seed maturation, causing kernels to sprout prematurely while still attached to the ear!
pathology: 'Wilty' Tomato Mutants (*flacca* and *sitiens*): Defective in Molybdenum cofactor sulfurase / aldehyde oxidase (the final step of ABA biosynthesis), causing permanently open stomata, rapid leaf wilting under mild low-humidity conditions, and full rescue upon foliar ABA spray.

node_zigzag_pti_eti_sar.title: Plant Immunity: The Zig-Zag Model (PTI vs. ETI), Hypersensitive Response (HR) & Systemic Acquired Resistance (SAR)
node_zigzag_pti_eti_sar.subtitle: FLS2/BAK1 Surface PRRs vs. Intracellular NB-LRR (TIR/CC-NLR) Resistosomes & Salicylic Acid NPR1 Redox Switch

metrics.tier1_pti: Surface PRRs: FLS2 (binds bacterial Flagellin flg22) + EFR (EF-Tu) + CERK1 (fungal Chitin) + BAK1 -> MAPK cascade, Callose, ROS burst
metrics.tier2_eti: Intracellular NLRs (Nucleotide-Binding Leucine-Rich Repeat R-proteins: TIR-NLR & CC-NLR [ZAR1 Ca2+ channel resistosome!]) -> Hypersensitive Response (HR)
metrics.flor_gene_for_gene: Incompatibility (Resistance / HR) occurs ONLY when Plant carries Dominant Resistance (R) allele AND Pathogen carries Dominant Avirulence (Avr) allele!
metrics.sar_mobile_axis: Local HR -> Salicylic Acid (SA via ICS1) + Mobile signals (Methyl Salicylate, Pipecolic/N-Hydroxypipecolic Acid, Azelaic Acid) -> Monomeric NPR1 enters nucleus -> PR1/PR2/PR5!

mechanism: **JONES & DANGL (2006) ZIG-ZAG MODEL OF PLANT IMMUNITY**:

1. **Phase 1 — PAMP-Triggered Immunity (PTI)**: Cell-surface Pattern Recognition Receptors (e.g., **FLS2**, which recognizes the conserved 22-aa N-terminal peptide **flg22** of bacterial flagellin and heterodimerizes with **BAK1**; or **CERK1**, which recognizes fungal **Chitin**) activate **BIK1 $\rightarrow$ RBOHD** (apoplastic ROS burst), **MPK3/MPK6** kinase cascade, **Callose** cell-wall reinforcement, and stomatal closure.

2. **Phase 2 — Effector-Triggered Susceptibility (ETS)**: Adapted pathogens inject **Effector proteins** (e.g., via the bacterial **Type III Secretion System [T3SS]** encoded by *hrp* genes) directly into the host cytoplasm to cleave or inhibit PTI components (like BAK1/BIK1/RIN4).

3. **Phase 3 — Effector-Triggered Immunity (ETI) & The Guard/Decoy Model**: Plants deploy intracellular **NLR (NB-LRR) Resistance (R) proteins** that either bind effectors directly or **'Guard'** host target proteins (e.g., the host guardee **RIN4** is guarded by two R-proteins: **RPM1** [senses RIN4 phosphorylation by AvrRpm1] and **RPS2** [senses RIN4 cleavage by the cysteine protease effector AvrRpt2]!). Activated CC-NLRs (like **ZAR1**) assemble into a pentameric **Resistosome** that inserts into the plasma membrane as a **$\text{Ca}^{2+}$-permeable channel**, triggering rapid programmed cell death (**Hypersensitive Response [HR]**) to quarantine biotrophic pathogens!

**SYSTEMIC ACQUIRED RESISTANCE (SAR — Whole-Plant Broad-Spectrum Memory)**: Following a local HR, **Salicylic Acid (SA)** accumulates (synthesized via chloroplastic **Isochorismate Synthase 1 [ICS1 / SID2]**) alongside phloem-mobile signals (**N-Hydroxypipecolic Acid [NHP]** and **Methyl Salicylate [MeSA]**). SA alters cellular redox potential (via Thioredoxins), reducing intermolecular disulfide bonds in the cytosolic oligomeric complex of **NPR1** so that **monomeric NPR1** translocates into the nucleus, binds **TGA** transcription factors (while SA also binds NPR3/NPR4), and activates **Pathogenesis-Related (*PR-1, PR-2 [$\beta$-1,3-glucanase], PR-5 [thaumatin]*)** defense genes throughout systemic uninoculated leaves!
csir_high_yield: Harold Flor's Gene-for-Gene Hypothesis Matrix (Guaranteed CSIR NET Part B & C Question!):

• **$R\text{ (Plant)} + Avr\text{ (Pathogen)}$** = **INCOMPATIBLE Interaction** $\rightarrow$ Plant is **RESISTANT** (Pathogen is Avirulent; rapid localized **Hypersensitive Response [HR]** lesions appear within 24h).

• **$R\text{ (Plant)} + avr\text{ (Pathogen)}$** OR **$r\text{ (Plant)} + Avr\text{ (Pathogen)}$** OR **$r\text{ (Plant)} + avr\text{ (Pathogen)}$** = **COMPATIBLE Interaction** $\rightarrow$ Plant is **SUSCEPTIBLE** (Pathogen is Virulent; spreading disease!).

• **Transgenic *NahG* Plants (Expressing Bacterial Salicylate Hydroxylase)**: Convert Salicylic Acid (SA) into inactive **Catechol**! *NahG* plants (and ***npr1-*** or ***sid2/ics1-*** mutants) **completely fail to establish Systemic Acquired Resistance (SAR)** and fail to express *PR-1*!
• **SAR vs. ISR (Induced Systemic Resistance)**:
– **SAR**: Triggered by local **pathogen necrosis / HR**; requires **Salicylic Acid (SA)** and **NPR1**; induces ***PR* genes**; effective against **Biotrophic pathogens**.

– **ISR**: Triggered by beneficial root-colonizing **PGPR (Plant Growth-Promoting Rhizobacteria** like *Pseudomonas fluorescens*); requires **Jasmonic Acid (JA) + Ethylene** (and cytosolic NPR1, *without* SA accumulation or *PR-1* induction!); primes defense against **Necrotrophs and Herbivores**.
pathology: Recessive Crop Susceptibility Gene (*mlo* & *xa13*) Editing: Because many biotrophic pathogens require host 'Susceptibility (*S*) genes' (e.g., powdery mildew requires barley **MLO**, and *Xanthomonas oryzae* TAL effectors induce rice **SWEET11/14** sugar effluxers to feed bacteria in the apoplast), CRISPR-Cas9 knockout of *MLO* or the *SWEET* promoter effector-binding element confers durable, broad-spectrum disease resistance!

metrics.sos_salt_pathway: High Soil Na+ -> MOCA1 (GIPC sphingolipid sensor) -> Ca2+ spike -> SOS3 (CBL4 Ca2+ sensor) -> SOS2 (CIPK24 kinase) -> SOS1 (PM Na+/H+ Antiporter!)
metrics.vacuolar_na_sequestration: NHX1 (Tonoplast Na+/H+ Antiporter driven by V-ATPase & V-PPase; sequesters Na+ inside vacuole!)
metrics.cold_acclimation_cascade: Chilling (4°C) -> ICE1 (bHLH TF, stabilized by OST1/SIZ1 SUMOylation) -> Transcribes CBF1/2/3 (DREB1) -> Bind CRT/DRE elements on COR genes!
metrics.compatible_solutes: Proline (synthesized via P5CS from Glutamate), Glycine Betaine (quaternary ammonium), Trehalose, Mannitol, Pinitol & LEA Dehydrins

mechanism: **1. THE SOS (SALT OVERLY SENSITIVE) PATHWAY FOR $\text{Na}^+$ HOMEOSTASIS**:
Excess cytosolic $\text{Na}^+$ (>100 mM) is toxic because $\text{Na}^+$ competes with essential $\text{K}^+$ binding sites on ribosomes and metabolic enzymes:
• Extracellular $\text{Na}^+$ binds plasma-membrane glycosyl inositol phosphorylceramide (**GIPC**) sphingolipids (synthesized by **MOCA1**), triggering a rapid cytosolic **$\text{Ca}^{2+}$ spike**.
• **SOS3 (CBL4)**—a myristoylated EF-hand calcium sensor—binds $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ and recruits the Ser/Thr protein kinase **SOS2 (CIPK24)** to the plasma membrane.

• The **SOS3–SOS2 complex phosphorylates the C-terminal autoinhibitory domain of SOS1**, activating **SOS1 (the Plasma-Membrane $\text{Na}^+/\text{H}^+$ Antiporter)** to pump $\text{Na}^+$ back out into the soil/apoplast (powered by the PM $\text{H}^+$-ATPase)! Simultaneously in shoots, **HKT1** unloads $\text{Na}^+$ from xylem vessels to protect photosynthetic leaves, while tonoplast **NHX1** pumps $\text{Na}^+$ into the **Vacuole** (turning toxic $\text{Na}^+$ into a cheap vacuolar osmoticum!).
**2. THE ICE1 – CBF/DREB1 – COR COLD ACCLIMATION CASCADE (ABA-Independent)**:

• Non-freezing chilling temperatures ($4^\circ\text{C}$) Rigidify plasma membranes $\rightarrow$ $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ influx + SUMOylation (by SIZ1) stabilizes the constitutive transcription factor **ICE1** (Inducer of CBF Expression 1).
• **ICE1** rapidly induces transcription of **CBF1, CBF2, and CBF3 (also called DREB1B, DREB1C, DREB1A)** within 15 minutes.

• **CBF/DREB1** proteins bind the **CRT/DRE (*C-Repeat / Dehydration-Responsive Element*, core `5'-CCGAC-3'`)** promoter motif (which is **ABA-INDEPENDENT**, distinct from the ABA-dependent ABRE motif commanded by AREB/ABF!) to induce **COR (*Cold-Regulated*)** genes and **LEA (*Late Embryogenesis Abundant*)** hydrophilic chaperone proteins that prevent membrane freeze-induced hexagonal-II phase transitions!
csir_high_yield: High-Yield CSIR NET Questions on Osmotic Adjustment, Proline & Flooding (*Sub1A*):

• **Water Potential Equation ($\Psi_w = \Psi_s + \Psi_p + \Psi_g$)**: For a root cell to continue absorbing water from dry or saline soil (where soil $\Psi_w$ is strongly negative, e.g., $-1.5\ \text{MPa}$), the plant cell must lower its intracellular **Solute/Osmotic Potential ($\Psi_s$)** even further without poisoning cytosolic enzymes!

• **Compartmentation Rule for Osmotic Adjustment**: Inorganic ions (**$\text{Na}^+$ and $\text{Cl}^-$**) are sequestered inside the **Central Vacuole** (via **NHX1**), whereas electrically neutral, non-toxic **Compatible Osmolytes** (**Proline** [synthesized from Glutamate via rate-limiting **$\Delta^1$-Pyrroline-5-Carboxylate Synthetase / P5CS**], **Glycine Betaine** [synthesized from Choline via CMO + BADH], and **Mannitol/Trehalose**) accumulate specifically in the **Cytosol and Chloroplast Stroma** to balance vacuolar osmotic pressure and stabilize hydration shells around proteins!
• **Submergence Tolerance vs. Escape in Rice (*Sub1A* vs. *SNORKEL1/2*)**:

– **Flash-Flood Tolerance (*Sub1A-1* gene in Swarna-Sub1 Rice)**: Ethylene trapped underwater induces the ERF transcription factor **Sub1A-1**, which upregulates DELLA (**SLR1**) to **SUPPRESS GA responsiveness and HALT shoot elongation underwater**, conserving carbohydrate reserves until floodwaters recede (**Quiescence Strategy**)!

– **Deepwater Rice Escape (*SNORKEL1 & SNORKEL2*)**: Trapped ethylene induces *SNORKEL1/2*, which stimulate **Gibberellin ($\text{GA}_1/\text{GA}_4$) synthesis** to drive rapid internode elongation (up to 25 cm/day!) so leaves stay above rising seasonal floodwaters (**Escape Strategy**), while cortical cells undergo ethylene/ROS-mediated programmed cell death to form lysigenous **Aerenchyma** gas channels!
pathology: Frost & Chilling Injury in Crops: Ice crystals almost always nucleate first in the **extracellular apoplast** (because apoplastic fluid has a much lower solute concentration and higher freezing point than the symplast!). Because liquid water inside the cell has a higher vapor pressure than extracellular ice, water is sucked out of the cytoplasm into the apoplast—meaning **freezing injury is fundamentally a severe cellular DEHYDRATION stress**!
lab_workbench: Bates Ninhydrin Colorimetric Proline Assay (at 520 nm in Toluene) & Electrolyte Leakage Assay: Quantifies cold/freeze membrane damage by measuring the electrical conductivity of deionized water bathing freeze-thawed leaf discs before and after autoclaving.

agents.name: Red (660 nm) Flash Followed Immediately by Far-Red (730 nm) Flash
agents.binding_site: Converts Phytochromobilin chromophore back from active C15-trans (Pfr) to inactive C15-cis (Pr)
agents.rescue_experiment: Classic Borthwick & Hendricks Experiment: In any R–FR–R–FR flash series, only the FINAL flash dictates the biological outcome! Ending with Far-Red converts Pfr back to inactive Pr, keeping PIFs and COP1 active (inhibiting lettuce seed germination and canceling the night-break effect!).

agents.name: NPA (1-N-Naphthylphthalamic Acid) / TIBA
agents.binding_site: Inhibits basal PIN1–7 and ABCB plasma-membrane auxin efflux carriers without blocking AUX1 influx
agents.rescue_experiment: Traps IAA anions inside cells (since neutral IAAH still enters from the acidic apoplast, but IAA- cannot exit without functional PIN carriers), pooling auxin at the shoot apex and completely abolishing gravitropic/phototropic bending and lateral root initiation!

agents.name: Paclobutrazol (ent-Kaurene Oxidase Inhibitor)
agents.binding_site: Inhibits ER cytochrome P450 ent-Kaurene Oxidase (blocks ent-kaurene -> ent-kaurenoic acid)
agents.rescue_experiment: Depletes endogenous bioactive GA1/GA4, leaving GID1 empty and allowing DELLA repressors (GAI/RGA/SLR1) to accumulate and arrest stem growth. Because GID1 and SCF^(SLY1) remain intact, spraying exogenous GA3 100% rescues the dwarf phenotype back to normal height!

agents.name: Silver Ions (Ag+ / STS) or 1-MCP in Dark + Ethylene
agents.binding_site: Displaces/locks the Cu+ cofactor in the transmembrane pocket of ETR1, keeping ETR1 & CTR1 permanently ON
agents.rescue_experiment: CSIR Epistasis Test: Ag+ or 1-MCP locks ETR1 in its active (CTR1-stimulating) conformation even in high ethylene or in an eto1 overproducer mutant, preventing the Triple Response. However, Ag+ CANNOT rescue a ctr1- loss-of-function mutant because CTR1 is downstream of the ETR1 receptor!

agents.name: Acute Drought / Abscisic Acid (50 µM ABA) Application
agents.binding_site: Binds PYR/PYL/RCAR receptors -> Plugs the catalytic active site of ABI1/ABI2 PP2C phosphatases
agents.rescue_experiment: Inhibits PP2C, unleashing OST1 (SnRK2.6) to phosphorylate and open SLAC1 anion channels. Massive Cl- and Malate2- efflux depolarizes the guard cell plasma membrane, opening GORK K+out channels and driving rapid osmotic water efflux and complete stomatal closure within 15 minutes!

quiz_challenges.prompt: Click the photoreceptor node where a phyA- mutant exhibits an elongated hypocotyl specifically under Continuous Far-Red light, whereas a phyB- mutant is elongated under Continuous Red light.
quiz_challenges.explanation: Correct! phyA (Type I, light-labile) mediates the Far-Red High Irradiance Response (FR-HIR), whereas phyB (Type II, light-stable) mediates Red-light de-etiolation and shade avoidance.

quiz_challenges.prompt: Click the hormone pathway where Green Revolution wheat (Rht) carries a dominant GA-insensitive DELLA mutation, whereas Green Revolution rice (sd1) carries a recessive GA20-oxidase biosynthetic mutation rescuable by spraying GA3.
quiz_challenges.explanation: Spot on! Wheat Rht lacks a functional N-terminal DELLA domain so GID1-GA cannot trigger its degradation (GA-insensitive), whereas Rice sd1 is deficient in GA 20-oxidase (GA-sensitive).

quiz_challenges.prompt: Click the ER-to-nucleus hormone pathway where the receptor (ETR1) and Raf-like kinase (CTR1) are ACTIVE in air (absence of hormone), and a ctr1- loss-of-function mutant shows a constitutive Triple Response.
quiz_challenges.explanation: Exact match! ETR1 and CTR1 are negative regulators active in the absence of ethylene; ethylene binding to ETR1's Cu+ cofactor turns OFF ETR1/CTR1, allowing EIN2-CEND cleavage and EIN3 stabilization.

quiz_challenges.prompt: Click the octadecanoid wound-hormone node hijacked by Pseudomonas syringae toxin Coronatine (a structural mimic of JA-Ile) to suppress Salicylic Acid immunity and reopen stomata.
quiz_challenges.explanation: Correct! Coronatine mimics (+)-7-iso-JA-Ile, binding the SCF^(COI1)-JAZ co-receptor to hyperactivate MYC2, which antagonizes the Salicylic Acid pathway and reopens stomata.
